sn12.33:1.2: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you forty-four cases of knowledge.
sn12.33:1.3: Listen to that and attend closely, I will speak.”
sn12.33:2.1: “Bhikkhus, what are the forty-four cases of knowledge?
sn12.33:2.2: Knowledge of aging-and-death, knowledge of its origin, knowledge of its cessation, knowledge of the way leading to its cessation.
sn12.33:2.9: Knowledge of the six sense bases …
sn12.33:2.12: Knowledge of volitional formations, knowledge of their origin, knowledge of their cessation, knowledge of the way leading to their cessation.
sn12.33:2.13: These, bhikkhus, are the forty-four cases of knowledge.
sn12.33:3.7: Thus this aging and this death are together called aging-and-death.
sn12.33:4.1: With the arising of birth there is the arising of aging-and-death.
sn12.33:4.2: With the cessation of birth there is the cessation of aging-and-death.
sn12.33:4.3: This Noble Eightfold Path is the way leading to the cessation of aging-and-death; that is,
sn12.33:5.1: “When, bhikkhus, a noble disciple thus understands aging-and-death, its origin, its cessation, and the way leading to its cessation, this is his knowledge of the principle.
sn12.33:5.2: By means of this principle that is seen, understood, immediately attained, fathomed, he applies the method to the past and to the future thus:
sn12.33:6.1: ‘Whatever ascetics and brahmins in the past directly knew aging-and-death, its origin, its cessation, and the way leading to its cessation, all these directly knew it in the very same way that I do now.
sn12.33:7.1: Whatever ascetics and brahmins in the future will directly know aging-and-death, its origin, its cessation, and the way leading to its cessation, all these will directly know it in the very same way that I do now.’
sn12.33:7.2: This is his knowledge of entailment.
sn12.33:8.1: “When, bhikkhus, a noble disciple has purified and cleansed these two kinds of knowledge—
sn12.33:8.2: knowledge of the principle and knowledge of entailment—
sn12.33:8.3: he is then called a noble disciple who is accomplished in view, accomplished in vision, who has arrived at this true Dhamma, who sees this true Dhamma, who possesses a trainee’s knowledge, a trainee’s true knowledge, who has entered the stream of the Dhamma, a noble one with penetrative wisdom, one who stands squarely before the door to the Deathless.
sn12.33:10.3: This Noble Eightfold Path is the way leading to the cessation of volitional formations; that is,
sn12.33:11.1: “When, bhikkhus, a noble disciple thus understands volitional formations, their origin, their cessation, and the way leading to their cessation, this is his knowledge of the principle.
sn12.33:11.2: By means of this principle that is seen, understood, immediately attained, fathomed, he applies the method to the past and to the future….
sn12.33:13.2: This is his knowledge of entailment.
sn12.33:14.1: “When, bhikkhus, a noble disciple has purified and cleansed these two kinds of knowledge—
sn12.33:14.2: knowledge of the principle and knowledge of entailment—
sn12.33:14.3: he is then called a noble disciple who is accomplished in view … one who stands squarely before the door to the Deathless.”
